name: Adelaide Plains

climate: Few classic table-wine grapes keep their freshness in heat like this. It suits fortified wine, table grapes and raisins.
Syrah is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Cabernet Sauvignon is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Pinot Gris is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Chardonnay is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.

soil.rock: Gravel drains fast and is poor, so roots go deep for water and food. It holds little water. Sand is warm and airy. It drains fast but holds little water, and phylloxera does not thrive in it.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its high pH can starve vines of iron and yellow the leaves, so growers plant lime-tolerant rootstocks.

land: Mostly flat. Easy and cheap to farm by machine, but on still nights cold air settles on flat ground, so spring frost is a bigger risk.

winkler: Big crops are possible, but quality tops out at acceptable.
